articles.title: Labour councils turn on Sadiq Khan’s housing plans
articles.summary: Khan has revised downwards his affordable homes quota
articles.ai_summary:
- Labour councils are rebelling against Sadiq Khan's housing plans after he reduced the quota for affordable homes.  
- This controversy highlights growing tensions within the party over housing strategies in London.

articles.title: Council to “engage” with landlords over tougher rental enforcement
articles.summary: The council is run jointly by the Greens and Labour
articles.ai_summary:
- The council, led by a coalition of the Greens and Labour, plans to initiate discussions with landlords regarding stricter rental enforcement regulations.  
- This move aims to enhance tenant protections and improve housing standards across the community.

articles.title: Labour MP blames landlords’ rents for size of welfare budget
articles.summary: Margaret Mullane is a Labour MP
articles.ai_summary:
- Labour MP Margaret Mullane targets landlords, claiming their high rents are a major contributor to the growing welfare budget.  
- The call for reform highlights the impact of rising housing costs on government spending and social support systems.

articles.title: Traitors winner says high rent makes it tough for first time buyers
articles.summary: Winning The Traitors doesn't mean you can afford to buy a home...
articles.ai_summary:
- Even after winning The Traitors, high rental costs pose a significant challenge for first-time buyers in the UK property market.  
- The disparity between rental prices and homeownership continues to hinder aspiring homeowners, regardless of newfound financial gains.

articles.title: Quick buy firm targets landlords quitting rental sector
articles.summary: The initiative follows the Renters Rights Act triggering many landlords to quit
articles.ai_summary:
- Quick buy firms are capitalizing on the exodus of landlords leaving the rental market due to the new Renters Rights Act.  
- The trend highlights increasing challenges for landlords, prompting many to sell their properties swiftly.

articles.title: Landlords to pay £11,713 bill per property to meet EPC rules
articles.summary: This is according to Landlord Trends research from Pegasus Insight
articles.ai_summary:
- Landlords face an average cost of £11,713 per property to comply with new Energy Performance Certificate (EPC) regulations, as highlighted by Pegasus Insight's Landlord Trends research.
- The rising financial burden emphasizes the growing challenges for landlords in adapting to stricter environmental standards in the UK property market.

articles.title: Renters Rights Act has no effect so far, claims agent
articles.ai_summary:
- A recent report by Foxtons indicates that the Renters Rights Act has had no noticeable impact on the rental market to date.
- Concerns are rising as agents highlight the lack of changes for renters despite the new legislation.

articles.title: Five lettings agency myths blown out of the water – apparently
articles.ai_summary:
- Lomond debunks five common myths about lettings agencies, challenging widely held misconceptions in the industry.  
- The revelations aim to provide clarity and elevate the reputation of lettings agencies among landlords and tenants alike.

articles.title: Renters Rights Act worsening affordability crisis – claim
articles.summary: The advice is given by one of the UK's leading lettings agency experts
articles.ai_summary:
- Experts warn that the Renters Rights Act may exacerbate the UK’s affordability crisis for tenants.  
- Increased regulations are seen as potentially driving up rental costs and reducing housing availability.

articles.title: Labour set to miss key house building target
articles.summary: The analysis has been undertaken by the agency and property consultancy Savills
articles.ai_summary:
- Labour is poised to fall short of its crucial house-building target, according to a recent analysis by Savills.  
- The findings highlight potential shortcomings in the government's housing strategy as the demand for homes continues to rise.

articles.title: Right To Rent code slammed for being too complex
articles.summary: The call for clarity has come from Propertymark
articles.ai_summary:
- Propertymark criticizes the Right to Rent code for its excessive complexity, urging the need for clearer guidelines.  
- The organization highlights that the convoluted nature of the code complicates the rental process for landlords and tenants alike.

articles.title: Renters Rights Act training sessions at landmark 100th show
articles.summary: It's in London on July 8, and entrance is free
articles.ai_summary:
- Landmark 100th Renters Rights Act training session set for July 8 in London, promoting awareness and education among tenants.  
- Free entrance to the event, making it accessible for all renters looking to empower themselves with knowledge of their rights.
